abstract: Evaluates facility seismic design tolerances, geotechnical stability, and structural containment integrity
system_message:
You are the Structural resilience engineer (STRUC), responsible for evaluating facility seismic design tolerances, geotechnical stability, and structural containment integrity across municipal water purification candidate designs.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Evaluates facility seismic design tolerances, geotechnical stability, and structural containment integrity（SEISMIC）
information_points.content:
STRUC-SEISMIC-QFX：For the Indirect aquifer recharge infiltration basin, structural and geotechnical assessments across all critical containment basins, pump stations, and chemical contact chambers establish a seismic peak ground acceleration tolerance of 0.6 g sustained without functional rupture.
STRUC-SEISMIC-NAY：For the Direct potable reuse multi-barrier train, structural calculations across all critical containment basins, pump stations, and chemical contact chambers confirm a seismic peak ground acceleration tolerance of 0.6 g sustained without functional rupture.
STRUC-SEISMIC-JPK：For the Engineered wetlands sequential treatment system, the structural design evaluation covering all critical containment basins, pump stations, and chemical contact chambers indicates a seismic peak ground acceleration tolerance of 0.45 g sustained without functional rupture.

information_points.title: Concrete durability analysis（CORROS）
information_points.content:
STRUC-CORROS-TCW：Materials testing for the Direct potable reuse multi-barrier train indicates a wet well concrete service life of 50 years prior to major rebar corrosion initiation for concrete contact basins exposed to chlorinated reclaimed water.
STRUC-CORROS-7WZ：Materials testing for the Indirect aquifer recharge infiltration basin projects a wet well concrete service life of 100 years prior to major rebar corrosion initiation for concrete contact basins exposed to chlorinated reclaimed water.
STRUC-CORROS-AVJ：Materials testing for the Engineered wetlands sequential treatment system projects a wet well concrete service life of 75 years prior to major rebar corrosion initiation for concrete contact basins exposed to chlorinated reclaimed water.
